correctness.rationale: All sixteen boundary-decorated sets consist of n-1 disjoint central horizontal matching edges and two disjoint endpoint edges. Endpoint coverage forces the remaining middle-row vertices and leaves top/bottom row intervals whose lengths are even iff the two endpoint phase labels agree. Thus eight mismatched-phase sets are nonextendable. Deleting a boundary edge admits substitution of the matching-phase vertical boundary edge; deleting any central spine edge allows oppositely oriented vertical edges at the two newly free middle-row vertices and horizontally even residual intervals. This constructs a perfect matching after every one-edge deletion for every integer n>=2. Distinctness, minimality, and degree n+1 follow. A standalone exhaustive DFS independently tests all sixteen cases and all one-edge deletions for 21 sample widths (2..18,20,25,30,40); computation corroborates, not proves, the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The new result constructs eight explicit size-n+1 inclusion-minimal nonextendable matchings for every n>=2 in width-three rectangular grids, proving unbounded forbidden-pattern arity and unbounded minimal Stanley–Reisner generator degree. The 2026 same-complex homotopy paper uses a similar spine and mentions three-edge bad matchings but does not state this boundary-phase family or the unbounded-size result in the inspected material; the 2024 two-row classification excludes width three. Published-result comparisons on finite three-row perfect matching complexes and signed domino tilings do not logically imply the claimed infinite family. Prior art on general minimal unextendable matchings may remain unlocated.

value.rationale: Minimal nonfaces are an intrinsic obstruction invariant and minimal squarefree generators of the Stanley–Reisner ideal. The result proves unbounded minimal-generator degree within the natural fixed-width 3×2n rectangular grid family, in contrast to the known width-two bound of degree two, exhibiting a sharp qualitative complexity jump. The 8 patterns are motivated by the same middle-row spine central to current homotopy work rather than an arbitrary finite slice; no unsupported complete census is asserted.
